scope: Three-temporal-clip-per-episode DROID View LoRA heldout evaluation
summary: Expanding every training episode to start/middle/end clips improves aggregate motion correlation but substantially regresses subject and scene consistency, so the route is rejected in favor of the earlier appearance-stronger candidate and neither is accepted.
evidence: Training completed 273/273 steps on physical A800 GPU 4 at rank 16, learning rate 2e-5, and seed 20260811.
The checkpoint is 21,908,240 bytes with SHA-256 e0d504a76f3bb61ebfcddffdf92013db7713b1cf6521fe296950c277b5a408d6.
All three heldout generations record real_target_passed_to_model=false and use the frozen 15-step recipe.
Aggregate motion correlation improves from -0.262506 to 0.374912, but full-frame SSIM falls from 0.520788 to 0.390229 and subject-ROI SSIM falls from 0.376567 to 0.270019.
Aggregate edge F1 is 0.316603 and static-anchor gain is -0.473055; every episode remains rejected.
Episode 60 additionally exceeds the motion-magnitude ceiling at 4.410914.
lessons: Temporal diversity helps the timing proxy but does not solve appearance-preserving cross-view geometry under raw wrist-pixel VACE control.
Model selection must keep subject consistency and motion as independent hard dimensions rather than trading one for the other.
limitations: The selected public candidate is still PARTIAL because its stronger appearance does not compensate for failed motion and static-anchor gates.
No route proves calibrated 3D viewpoint synthesis or physical robot execution.
next_actions: Replace raw wrist-pixel spatial control with a cross-view motion representation or calibrated camera/action conditioning before another promotion attempt.
